Current density identified 19 pathogenic controls with loss of function, while gating and recovery from inactivation identified additional abnormal variants with preserved or partially preserved current density. The assay generated likelihood ratios of 0.033 for normal function and 25.13 for abnormal function, supporting BS3 and PS3 functional evidence, respectively. Application to 23 CACNA1A variants identified in Australian patients showed abnormal function in all four variants already classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Among 19 variants of uncertain significance, 11 were functionally abnormal and nine were reclassified as likely pathogenic after integration of PS3 evidence with other ACMG/AMP criteria. These data show that CACNA1A missense variants can produce loss-of-function, gain-of-function or mixed effects, and that multi-parameter functional assessment is required for accurate interpretation. This calibrated automated patch-clamp framework provides clinically interpretable evidence for refining CACNA1A variant classification in diagnostic practice.
ncbccc6dc76de: To evaluate the clinical implementation of long-read genome sequencing (lrGS) and establish the population reference resources needed to support its use in diagnostics, we integrate two complementary initiatives: Genome of Sweden (GoS), Sweden's contribution to Genome of Europe (GoE), and the Genomic Medicine Sweden - Rare Diseases (GMS-RD) long-read sequencing pilot. The initial GoS release of 576 individuals provides population-scale maps of genetic and epigenetic variation. Among 485 GMS-RD probands, 161 (33.2%) receive a molecular diagnosis, with lrGS providing added clinical value in 40 (24.8%). As a first-line test, lrGS could have avoided at least 42 follow-up analyses and an additional testing cycle in 7.2% of probands, reducing costs and the burden on patients. By integrating population and clinical long-read genomics, Sweden establishes a national ecosystem for genomic research and clinical diagnostics. Our findings support the clinical implementation of lrGS and offer a scalable model for national collaboration.
nddaee23194a4: Objectives: To assess the feasibility and early performance of an AI-assisted screening workflow that reviews inpatient discharge summaries to identify potential treatment injuries for clinician review and, where appropriate, Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) treatment injury claim consideration in New Zealand. Design: Single-site, six-month pilot reported as a quality-improvement/service-evaluation activity. A large language model (LLM)-enabled system acted as an index screening test over discharge summaries to generate candidate treatment injury signals for structured clinician adjudication and escalation. Setting: A New Zealand district hospital (Wairarapa). Screening operated on routinely produced inpatient discharge summaries. Participants: All inpatient discharge summaries produced during the pilot period were screened (n = 2,642). The unit of analysis was one discharge summary per inpatient episode. Intervention: An LLM-based screening workflow that outputs structured candidate harm signals with supporting excerpts and a certainty label. Outputs were reviewed by clinicians using a structured adjudication template. Suitable cases could be escalated to senior clinicians and followed through the local ACC treatment injury process. Main outcome measures: Primary outcomes were yield, positive predictive value (PPV) of AI- flagged signals for clinician-adjudicated iatrogenic harm, and the rate of unsupported/hallucinated outputs. Secondary outcomes included overlap with incident reporting and administrative coding, downstream ACC claim outcomes, and clinician review workload. Results: Across 2,642 inpatient discharge summaries screened, the AI-assisted workflow generated 237 candidate signals (yield 9.0%; 95% CI 7.9% to 10.1%). Clinician adjudication classified 102 as confirmed iatrogenic harm, 43 as possible harm requiring additional context, 81 as no harm, and 11 as unsupported/hallucinated outputs. PPV for confirmed harm was 43.0% (95% CI 36.8% to 49.4%). PPV for confirmed-or-possible harm was 61.2% (95% CI 54.9% to 67.1%). Seven ACC treatment injury claims were lodged as a direct result of AI-assisted surfacing; three were accepted, two declined, and two were held/pending at analysis. Organisational ACC data identified 68 treatment injury claims lodged during the same period, of which 17 overlapped with AI-identified cases. Conclusions: AI-assisted screening of discharge summaries can feasibly increase detection of potential treatment injuries for structured clinician review and may support more systematic ACC consideration and safety learning. Safe scaling requires transparent reporting of model and prompt details, robust human adjudication and escalation pathways, and governance controls to mitigate false positives and unsupported outputs. A next-stage evaluation should estimate diagnostic accuracy against a chart-review reference standard and examine implementation outcomes including workload, acceptability, fidelity and sustainability.
n70dd7064b9a5: Background This study presents reference ranges for cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived myocardial strain from the Healthy Hearts Consortium, while evaluating variations by demographic characteristics (age, sex, and ethnicity) and technical factors (scanner vendor, magnetic field strength). We derived reference ranges and centile-based categories for ventricular, atrial, and rapid strain parameters. The prognostic relevance of these categories was assessed by examining their associations with incident cardiovascular events. Methods The dataset included 9,088 CMR studies. Automated image analysis pipelines were established using suiteHEART (NeoSoft Inc.) and cvi42 (Circle Cardiovascular Imaging). A three-step quality control framework was applied including exclusion of incomplete data, visual assessment of image and segmentation quality, and statistical outlier removal. Ventricular strain and strain rate were measured using both software solutions. Additional cvi42 derived metrics included velocity and displacement, annular plane systolic excursion metrics, and rapid strain parameters. Age- and sex-specific reference ranges were generated using lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) modeling with penalized splines. Reference ranges were defined as values between the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. For lower-tail classification, values below the 2.5th percentile were considered mildly out-of-range and values below the 0.5th percentile at least moderately out-of-range. Differences across scanner vendors (Siemens, Philips, GE) and magnetic field strengths (1.5 T vs. 3 T) were evaluated using adjusted linear models. The prognostic relevance of selected cvi42-derived categories was evaluated in approximately 45,000 UK Biobank participants using Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Results After quality control, 8,975 CMR examinations (cvi42) and 8,992 (suiteHEART) were available for analysis; these represent software-specific analytic cohorts. Most exclusions occurred during visual quality control. Women had higher absolute ventricular and atrial strain values than men across all age groups. Left ventricular (LV) longitudinal strain and strain rate were slightly lower in older ages, whereas circumferential and radial parameters remained largely stable. Left atrial strain was also lower in older age groups, while right atrial strain did not vary by age. Annular plane systolic excursion and rapid strain metrics showed similar sex-specific patterns, with modestly lower atrial and displacement values in older groups. Ethnicity-related differences were modest, heterogeneous, and substantially smaller in magnitude than age- and sex-related differences. Technical effects were parameter specific. While LV longitudinal and circumferential strains were largely unaffected, radial strain was higher at 3 T and showed vendor-related differences. LMS-derived reference ranges and centile thresholds were applied both across all ethnicities and within ethnicity-specific analyses, and are presented stratified by age and sex. In the prognostic analysis, centile categories were most consistently associated with incident heart failure. LV longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain below the 0.5th centile were associated with significantly increased risk of incident heart failure (HRs: 9.9 to 12.4, 95% CIs 7.00-13.90 to 8.49-18.06). Conclusion This study provides age- and sex-specific reference ranges and centile-based categories for CMR-derived strain parameters in a large reference population. Age and sex represent the primary determinants of myocardial deformation, whereas scanner-related effects are parameter-specific. Values in the lower extremes of the healthy reference distribution, particularly for LV strain, are associated with increased risk of incident heart failure.…
nc788fa94a492: Objectives: Social media trends such as the "Benadryl Challenge" have increased adolescent misuse of diphenhydramine (DPH), an over-the-counter antihistamine with anticholinergic activity. Whether co-ingested anticholinergic medications compound cardiac risk is untested. Using the Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) scale, this study examined whether co-medication ACB burden is associated with outcome severity and cardiac toxicity in adolescent DPH cases reported to the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS). Methods: This study extracted all adolescent reports (age 13-19) mentioning DPH in any drug role from AEMS, yielding 3,168 cases from 217,507 deduplicated records. Given non-normality (Shapiro-Wilk, all p < 0.001), non-parametric tests were used. A multivariable logistic regression predicted cardiac toxicity; logistic and random-forest models were compared by cross-validated AUC. Results: Co-medication ACB burden correlated positively with case severity ({rho} = 0.142, p < 0.001) and differed by age group (H = 19.52, p < 0.001). However, burden and cardiac risk diverged: cardiac cases carried a lower burden (mean 0.55 vs 1.27) and were younger, and burden did not independently predict cardiac toxicity (OR = 0.927, 95% CI [0.841, 1.022], p = 0.128). Younger age was the strongest predictor (OR = 0.865 per year, p < 0.001); cardiac events occurred in 10.2% of 13-15-year-olds versus 4.9% of older adolescents. Conclusion: Anticholinergic co-medication burden and cardiac risk dissociate: burden tracks overall severity, but cardiac events concentrate in the youngest, least co-medicated adolescents, a profile consistent with deliberate single-agent overdose rather than polypharmacy. A low co-medication burden should not reassure clinicians triaging young adolescents.
na52c9758fe6d: Background: Childhood experiences contribute to health and wellbeing across the life course, yet research from low- and middle-income countries has largely focused on a few outcomes rather than broader patterns of adult wellbeing, behaviors, and social and financial circumstances. Methods: In this cross-sectional analysis, we used a nationally representative sample of adults in India (N = 12,765; aged [≥] 18 years) from the Global Flourishing Study (GFS) Wave 1 (2023) to examine associations between eight retrospectively reported childhood experience items, 45 adult outcomes, and two composite flourishing indices. Survey-weighted linear, logistic, and proportional-odds models adjusted for age, gender, education, and residential setting, with Bonferroni correction were used to assess associations and effect modification by gender. Findings: Although the breadth and strength of associations differed across childhood experiences, less favorable childhood experiences were generally associated with poorer wellbeing and flourishing, greater odds of adverse health outcomes, and reduced access to resources and safety in adult life. However, outcomes related to prosocial behaviors showed a different pattern: childhood abuse (physical or sexual) was associated with greater odds of volunteering (OR 1.31, 95% confidence interval or CI [1.13,1.51]), feeling like an outsider in one's family with greater odds of donating (OR 1.80, 95% CI [1.52,2.13]), volunteering (OR 1.53, 95% CI [1.28,1.82]), and helping a stranger (OR 1.49, 95% CI [1.27,1.74]). Associations were broadly similar between females and males, with little evidence of gender differences. Interpretation: Associations of childhood adversity with poorer health and increased prosocial behavior in adult life may reflect unmeasured social, cultural, or dispositional factors and heterogeneous life-course responses. Nevertheless, these findings support strengthening child-protection, financial assistance programs, and mental health services in India.
n1a1a552c8e80: Rationale: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is sustained by electrical triggers and atrial substrate, but whether AF itself generates circulating factors that acutely reinforce arrhythmogenesis is unknown. Objective: To determine whether rhythm-dependent serum bioactivity directly destabilizes atrial electrophysiology and to identify associated cellular mechanisms and circulating mediators. Methods and Results: Cardiac samples were obtained from patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) during AF and after restoration of sinus rhythm (SR) using electrical cardioversion. In isolated Langendorff-perfused mouse hearts, AF serum increased the duration, frequency, and cumulative burden of spontaneous atrial depolarizations compared with paired control perfusate. In human induced pluripotent stem cell derived atrial cardiomyocytes, AF patient serum decreased Ca2-transient amplitudes without significant effect on kinetics or Ca2 spark activity. Moreover, AF serum reduced peak sodium current without materially altering voltage-dependent gating or paced action-potential properties. Data-independent acquisition proteomics identified rhythm-associated changes in extracellular-matrix, proteolytic, inflammatory, and signaling proteins, including MMP9, Ccathepsin G, and 14-3-3 family members. Targeted pathway perturbation differentially modified serum-induced Ca2 phenotypes, indicating context-dependent, multifactorial bioactivity. Serum-induced Ca2 responses were not associated with indices of atrial disease severity, including low-voltage substrate burden and left atrial pressure. Conclusions: Persistent AF is accompanied by rhythm-dependent circulating bioactivity that acutely promotes atrial electrical instability and Ca2-dependent trigger formation. These findings extend the concept that AF begets AF beyond tissue-intrinsic remodeling and identify a potentially reversible serum-mediated feed-forward mechanism linking rhythm status and circulating proteomic signals in an atrial substrate severity independent fashion. Keywords: atrial fibrillation; serum; atrial cardiomyopathy; calcium signaling; circulating factors; proteomics
na5d4b68c4bce: HER2-directed therapies are expanding across solid tumors, but ERBB2 amplification incompletely captures HER2 expression and pan-tumor IHC lacks standardization. We developed ERBB2 mRNA, bulk HER2 protein and RNA-signature screening benchmarked against IHC/FISH. Screening identified HER2-enriched populations beyond amplification in a pan-tumor discovery cohort of 1,331 tumor biopsies and validated RNA-based screening in an external cohort of 3,898 tumor biopsies. All six objective responses among 51 treated patients in the discovery cohort occurred in tumors positive by ERBB2 mRNA and the combined RNA-signature. In the external dataset (n=102), ERBB2 mRNA positivity was associated with longer time on treatment (hazard ratio 0.42, 95% confidence interval 0.27-0.64) and overall survival (0.41, 0.25-0.65), with concordant associations for the combined RNA signature. Spatial proteomics comprising 2,721 tiles across 88 samples captured HER2 hetero-geneity and identified HER2-enriched profiles below bulk thresholds. These findings support prospective evaluation of RNA and proteomic screening for treatment selection.
nd9f6618ab526: Background: Cancer patients face a significantly elevated risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Although vaccination is a cornerstone of prevention, data on vaccination coverage and association with survival among Russian cancer patients remain scarce. We assessed COVID-19 vaccination coverage and its association with overall survival in a population-based cohort of cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Methods: This retrospective registry-based cohort study integrated data from the Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) of the Arkhangelsk Region and the Nenets Autonomous Okrug, regional vaccination records, and an artificial intelligence (AI)-based analysis of chest computed tomography (CT) scans. The cohort consisted of 1,144 cancer patients who underwent CT between August 2020 and April 2021. Vaccination status was ascertained via data linkage. Overall survival (OS) was compared between vaccinated and unvaccinated patients using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression, adjusted for demographic, clinical, and AI-derived CT biomarkers. To mitigate immortal time bias, the primary analysis used a landmark approach restricted to patients alive on March 1, 2021 (N = 1,136). A sensitivity analysis used a November 1, 2021 landmark (N = 894). Vaccination status was defined as receipt of at least one dose before the landmark date. Results: Only 6.6% (n=76) of patients received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine (Sputnik V or Sputnik Light). Vaccinated patients were more likely to have earlier-stage cancer and were less likely to be receiving active treatment. In the primary landmark analysis, vaccination was associated with a significantly higher 3‑year OS (80.3% vs. 45.7%, p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, vaccination was independently associated with a 60% lower hazard of all‑cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.64). AI-detected COVID-19 pneumonia on baseline CT was also an independent predictor of poorer survival (adjusted HR 1.32, 95% CI 1.09-1.59). In the sensitivity analysis (November 1, 2021 landmark), the adjusted HR for vaccination was 0.56 (95% CI 0.34-0.92), showing a consistent but attenuated association. Conclusion: This study reveals critically low COVID-19 vaccination coverage among cancer patients in Northwest Russia. Nevertheless, vaccination was strongly associated with a substantial survival benefit, underscoring its importance as a potentially lifesaving intervention for this vulnerable population.
n6f559f65d956: **Importance** Average gray matter volume (GMV) loss in early psychosis may conceal clinically relevant differences in brain change. **Objective** To identify longitudinal GMV-change patterns, their cross-site correspondence, and clinical associations. **Design, Setting, and Participants** Prospective cohort with T1-weighted MRI acquired during 2011-2026 at 2 Czech sites; median follow-up, approximately 13 months. Participants were 222 patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis and 178 healthy controls frequency-matched by site and baseline age. **Exposure** First-episode psychosis vs healthy control status. **Main Outcomes and Measures** Diagnosis-blind clustering by site of image-quality-corrected, subsequently annualized GMV change across 333 cortical parcels; longitudinal voxel-based morphometry (VBM); Global Assessment of Functioning and consensus 5-factor Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale negative-symptom scores. **Results** Among 400 participants (mean [SD] age, 28.2 [7.5] years), 208 (52.0%) were male. Each site independently yielded 3 clusters: C1 (near-stable GMV), C2 (pronounced decrease), and C3 (increase). Cross-site centroid correlations across 333 parcels were strong for C2 and C3 (Spearman rho = 0.865 and 0.861); C1 correlation was weak (rho = 0.138), as expected for near-zero profiles with little regional variation. C2/C3 correspondence supported pooling matched site-specific clusters for post hoc analyses. Pooled clusters contained 77 patients and 125 controls in C1, 66 patients and 16 controls in C2, and 79 patients and 37 controls in C3. Suffixes -P and -HC identify patient and control subgroups. To situate patient changes relative to controls, post hoc VBM revealed an unanticipated gradient of increasingly pronounced GMV reduction across C1-HC to C1-P to C2-P, prominently involving association cortex, and bilateral ventral temporal GMV increase in C3-P (familywise error-corrected P < .05). The opposite contrast along this ordering showed periventricular changes consistent with progressively greater ventricular enlargement. C2-P had the lowest mean follow-up functioning and highest mean negative-symptom severity (adjusted omnibus P = .005 and .02); clinical changes from baseline did not differ significantly among patient groups. **Conclusions and Relevance** Early GMV change in psychosis was not uniform but comprised two contrasting directions: a clinically relevant, control-anchored pattern of increasingly pronounced GMV loss involving default mode regions and a distinct, directionally opposing ventral temporal increase.
n615a7922f1a3: Background: Patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in intensive care units (ICUs) frequently receive antibiotics early in critical illness. Such exposure reflects suspected infection, physiological deterioration, monitoring intensity, and clinical management and may vary across institutions and electronic health record databases. We evaluated target-domain adaptation for modeling sustained antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with ICH. Methods: We analyzed derived ICH cohorts from MIMIC-IV and the eICU Collaborative Research Database. MIMIC-IV included 2,024 ICU stays and served as the source cohort. The eICU cohort comprised 1,277 stays and was divided, at the ICU-stay level, into a development subset (766 stays) and a held-out evaluation subset (511 stays). The eICU outcome was sustained antibiotic exposure on at least two ICU days. Candidate models incorporated demographic, comorbidity, physiological, laboratory, neurologic, respiratory, temporal, and measurement-process features. Timestamped observations for static and temporal tabular families were censored at the recorded first-antibiotic time when available, whereas the compact sequence component and explicit measurement-density features used the full first 24 hours. For base-model families using eICU development data, meta-learner inputs were generated by five-fold stratified cross-fitting. A 42-input L2-penalized logistic meta-learner combined 16 model probabilities with model-summary, clinical, availability, and measurement-density features. Results: The held-out eICU subset contained 48 positive outcomes (9.39%). The adapted ensemble achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.841 (95% CI 0.775-0.899) and an average precision (AP) of 0.540 (95% CI 0.399-0.676), with a Brier score of 0.063 and expected calibration error of 0.029. The MIMIC-IV source-only stack achieved an AUROC of 0.782; the paired AUROC difference was 0.059 (95% CI 0.003-0.112). In a separate patient-grouped five-fold out-of-fold sensitivity analysis of 503 linked eICU stays, AUROC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.691-0.910). Conclusions: Target-domain adaptation improved held-out discrimination relative to a source-only stack for sustained antibiotic exposure. Because some model components and measurement-process features used information from the broader first 24 hours, the model should be interpreted as a first-24-hour treatment-association model rather than a strictly prospective pre-treatment infection predictor.
n00a208152e40: Background: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is associated with high early mortality. Although routine coagulation markers are clinically relevant, their incremental value for mortality prediction beyond neurologic and physiologic information is uncertain. We developed and externally validated models using first-24-hour ICU data and evaluated the added predictive value of routine coagulation measurements. Methods: We used MIMIC-IV for model development and eICU-CRD for external validation. The development cohort included 2,669 adults with non-traumatic ICH and 388 ICU deaths. Logistic regression, random forest, and XGBoost were evaluated using a patient-level 70:30 holdout split and 5-fold stratified cross-validation. External validation used a high-specificity primary eICU cohort (396 patients; 39 deaths) and a broader secondary hemorrhagic-stroke/likely-ICH cohort (1,555 patients; 168 deaths). Performance was assessed using AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score, calibration, and paired bootstrap comparisons. GCS-only and age-plus-GCS models served as clinical benchmarks. Coagulation-only, clinical-only, and combined XGBoost models were compared to assess incremental value. Results: In the internal holdout cohort, AUROCs were 0.870 for logistic regression, 0.859 for random forest, and 0.867 for XGBoost. In the primary external cohort, corresponding AUROCs were 0.804, 0.839, and 0.817; AUPRCs were 0.342, 0.419, and 0.406; and Brier scores were 0.080, 0.072, and 0.074. In the broader cohort, AUROCs were 0.826, 0.848, and 0.838. Random forest showed the numerically strongest external performance, but pairwise AUROC differences among multivariable models were not clearly supported. GCS-only achieved AUROCs of 0.780 and 0.813 in the primary and broader cohorts. Coagulation-only XGBoost showed weak discrimination (AUROC 0.598 internally, 0.598 primary external, and 0.566 broader external). Adding coagulation variables to the clinical model produced AUROC differences of 0.014 (95% CI -0.009 to 0.037) and 0.003 (95% CI -0.007 to 0.013) in the two external cohorts. Conclusions: Multivariable models based on first-24-hour ICU data retained useful discrimination across external cohorts and provided modest gains over simple GCS-based benchmarks. Routine coagulation markers alone were weak predictors and did not provide clearly supported incremental discrimination beyond broader clinical information. Cross-database transportability should be interpreted together with phenotype alignment and calibration.
n394a1d03a55a: Background: Estimating nutrient intake from meal photographs with vision-language models (VLMs) is now practical, but patient photographs often cannot leave the institution. We developed PLANS (Personal-device Local Assessment of Nutrients System), in which a small open VLM runs entirely on a personal device. Methods: Open VLMs were compared on two image sets with reference values (NutriImage, 887 Japanese meals; SNAPMe, 1,134 US meals), and the selected model (Qwen3-VL-4B, 4-bit) was run on an iPad Air without network access. Energy (primary outcome), protein, fat, carbohydrate and salt were evaluated by median absolute percentage error (MedAPE) and Spearman rank correlation (rho). The effect of supplying the food weight, including errors in it, was examined. Results: Energy estimates on the iPad were identical to those of a desktop-computer run for 84-86% of images (other values, 75-87%). MedAPE on the iPad was 37.0% and 36.5% for energy (26-28% of images within +/-20%), 43-65% for the macronutrients and 68-101% for salt (rho 0.51-0.85). On the desktop computer, supplying the true weight reduced MedAPE of the 4B model on NutriImage from 37.0% to 32.5% for energy and from 100.0% to 66.8% for salt; energy MedAPE stayed below the base value for declared weights of 0.5-1.25 times the true weight or rounded to 50 g, but rose markedly when the container weight was included. Conclusions: An offline VLM on a tablet reproduced server-side energy accuracy and is a candidate tool for dietary counselling where photographs cannot leave the institution; given the wide limits of agreement, its usefulness in practice remains to be examined.
nd21789210d09: The hippocampus has long been implicated in depression, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Leveraging precision functional mapping in densely sampled individuals and large cross-sectional cohorts, and validating key results in direct intracranial EEG recordings from the human brain, we show that hippocampal connectivity alternates between two discrete and opposing network states on the order of minutes: one dominated by default mode network (DMN) coupling and another by sensorimotor system (SM) coupling. This dynamic switching is a fundamental property of hippocampal function in both healthy brains and in major depressive disorder (MDD). In MDD, this equilibrium is disrupted, such that the DMN-dominant state is overrepresented. In densely sampled individuals, hippocampus-DMN coupling tracks symptom fluctuations over time and normalizes after electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), which drives switches in hippocampal connectivity away from the DMN-dominant state and toward the SM-dominant state, an effect that was closely linked to a positive treatment response. Direct intracranial recordings in patients with MDD identified analogous fluctuations in hippocampal-DMN theta synchrony, which tracks symptom fluctuations over hours and days. Together, these findings identify a dynamic cortico-hippocampal mechanism underlying depression and indicate that successful neuromodulation treatments such as ECT act in part by restoring a dynamic equilibrium in hippocampal network connectivity.
na1fa16e2c094: Background: Vision-language models (VLMs) are being considered for estimating energy intake from meal photographs. Prompt descriptions such as a Japanese-dietitian persona shift the estimates, suggesting their use for calibration; what the estimates rest on was unknown. Objective: We examined whether prompt descriptions can serve as calibration, at which training stage responses to a nationality persona and to an amount instruction arise, and whether estimates follow the visible amount or one associated with the identified dish. Methods: Eleven commercial and 15 open-weight models were evaluated on NutriImage (887 Japanese single-dish photographs) and SNAPMe (1,134 US meal photographs) under eight prompt conditions (no description, five personas, and smaller- or larger-portion instructions). With one model, images were cropped or replaced by the dish name. Before- and after-meal photographs of 804 meals (ACETADA) were estimated. Pre-trained and post-trained weights of Gemma 3 and InternVL3.5 8B were compared by likelihood scoring. Prompts were compared with numerical calibration. Results: Where the dish was named as in the full image, a 25% crop changed neither the median absolute percentage error (MedAPE; 33.8% vs 34.4%) nor the persona shift (-20 vs -20 kcal); dish names alone gave similar accuracy (MedAPE 31.7%); nearly empty trays still received 39%-75% of the before-meal estimate, often described as already eaten. Between models, the persona shift was related to baseline bias (r = -0.77) and less to instruction following (r = -0.36); the instruction shift showed the reverse (r = -0.14 and -0.95). In Gemma 3, the Japan-US contrast was 2-4 times larger before post-training, and the instruction response 2-4 times larger after it (InternVL3.5 8B: 3 and 1.4 times). Across images, the Japan-US contrast was uniform on US meals and, for Japanese dishes in the commercial models, Gemma 3, and Qwen3-VL 32B, larger where overestimated. In these models, the persona lowered MedAPE for Japanese dishes as much as, or slightly more than, subtracting the mean bias, and no more than dividing by a ratio; on US meals it did not; in open-weight families that responded little, only numerical calibration lowered error. The smaller-portion instruction raised MedAPE in models with little bias (eg, 30.0% to 50.2%). Conclusions: In the model examined most closely, the estimates behaved as if anchored on an amount associated with the identified dish and only partly corrected by the visible amount. Prompt descriptions moved them by amounts depending on model and cuisine, not on the correction needed; a persona is therefore not proposed as a general means of calibration. In a facility, the findings suggest showing the identified dish for correction, calibrating by a ratio measured on reference meals with the deployed model, keeping amount statements out of the prompt, and not deriving intake from before-after-meal differences.
nd2408f61bc91: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) are common conditions in the general population. Several therapeutic approaches are available, but there is no consensus on the most effective, particularly in physiotherapy. Objectives: To assess the efficacy of manual therapy (MT) and therapeutic exercise (TE) in reducing pain in patients with TMDs. Methods: Four databases (MEDLINE, PEDro, EMBASE, CINAHL) were searched up to March 2025. We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the effects of MT and/or TE in individuals with TMDs, compared to any other rehabilitation treatment, with pain intensity as the primary outcome. The methodological quality was assessed using the PEDro scale. A network meta-analysis was performed to compare the effectiveness of different rehabilitative approaches. Results: 25 RCTs for a total of 1,540 people were included. The main comparisons were: MT and/or TE vs no treatment or placebo, occlusal splint, and instrumental physiotherapy. In most studies, MT and TE were more effective than controls in reducing pain. However, the network meta-analysis indicated that multimodal treatments were the most effective. The methodological quality of the included studies ranged from 3 to 9 points. Conclusion: MT and TE are effective strategies for reducing pain in subjects with TMDs and should be used as first-line interventions before more invasive treatments; the combination of dry needling and manual therapy appears to be the most effective approach. Nonetheless, the variability in study quality suggests that further high-quality research is needed to confirm these findings.
na9fae2b56a34: Bordetella pertussis is the main aetiological agent of pertussis (whooping cough), with a global resurgence of cases reported in 2024. As current pertussis diagnostics are predominantly based on molecular methods, cultured isolates are increasingly scarce, limiting traditional culture-based surveillance. To address these challenges, this study evaluated culture-independent approaches for B. pertussis surveillance and their feasibility for implementation in public health laboratory settings in Victoria, Australia. The Microbiological Diagnostic Unit Public Health Laboratory received 356 nasopharyngeal clinical specimens that were PCR-positive for Bordetella spp. from diagnostic laboratories for further characterisation during the 2024-2025 epidemic period. Culture-based approaches yielded only five B. pertussis isolates, largely due to limitations associated with specimen transport media. Four culture-independent approaches were evaluated for B. pertussis characterisation: real-time PCR assay for high-resolution Bordetella spp. differentiation (n=356), multiplex PCR amplicon sequencing assay for lineage typing (n=38), in-house laboratory developed test implemented on Panther Fusion(R) System for macrolide resistance screening (n=92) and shotgun metagenomic sequencing (n=5). The dataset was dominated by B. pertussis (330/356; 92.7%) with most strains harbouring ptxP3 (35/38; 92.1%) allele and the macrolide resistance rate was reported as 4.3% (4/92). Shotgun metagenomics was able to detect B. pertussis directly from clinical samples, but the genomic recovery was limited. Evaluation of operational performance and workflow integration highlighted method-specific strengths and limitations, informing suitability for implementation in public health laboratories. This study demonstrates the potential to integrate culture-independent approaches into public health laboratory settings to strengthen B. pertussis surveillance and inform feasible workflow design amid limited culture availability.
nd9f8200ace36: Introduction: Resection margins in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) are frequently inadequate. This study investigated the accuracy and diagnostic performance of ex-vivo 7T MRI against histology. Methods: Fifty OSCC specimens underwent ex-vivo 7T MRI. Tumours were segmented on corresponding histology and twice on MRI: blinded to histology (radiologist segmentation; clinical practice) and using histology (histology-MR segmentation; MR-based ground truth). Resection margins were measured in five regions and compared with histology. Results: Anterior and posterior margins were generally smaller on MRI than on histology (maximum mean difference -2.5 mm), whereas cranial, caudal and deep margins were generally larger on MRI (mean differences <1 mm). For close margins (<5 mm), sensitivity was 95% for histology-MR segmentations and 91% for radiologist segmentations, with 75% specificity for both. Conclusion: Ex-vivo 7T MRI accurately measures resection margins and detects close margins with high sensitivity. A future clinical trial will determine whether intraoperative implementation reduces inadequate margins and adjuvant treatment.
n9f4e973bf769: Clinical foundation models learn patterns in longitudinal health records that can be reused across prediction tasks. However, the relative strengths of representation-based and generation-based prediction across clinical tasks remain unclear. Using longitudinal electronic health records from 3.77 million patients at a single hospital, we developed FERMAT (Foundation model for Exploring Real-world Multimodal health data using Autoregressive Trajectory modeling), a 65-million-parameter clinical foundation model. We compared predictions from task-specific predictors trained on patient representations with those derived from generated clinical event sequences. Representation-based prediction performed better in the disease-risk comparisons. In detailed analyses of five-year chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, and diabetes risk in a test cohort of 10,000 patients, representation-based predictors exceeded generation-based estimates by 0.098-0.115 in observation-weighted AUROC and had lower probability error. Generation-based prediction, in turn, performed better in predicting diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures recorded on the same day, a task motivated by the frequent presence of multiple events with the same date in hospital EHRs. Using 50 generated trajectories per patient, it achieved a Recall@10 of 71.0%, compared with 55.7% for representation-based prediction, with a paired improvement of 15.31 percentage points (95% CI, 13.92-16.79; n = 1,862). These findings demonstrate task-dependent strengths of representation-based and generation-based applications within a single clinical foundation model, providing an empirical basis for exploring how the two approaches can be used individually or combined to address clinical prediction needs.
n23a2bb656531: Introduction Reliable, well-maintained laboratory equipment is essential for timely, accurate and reliable laboratory results for patient care, surveillance, and health system resilience. Tanzania implemented the Standard Medical Laboratory Equipment Guideline (SMLEG-2018) to harmonise procurement and improve efficiency across a tiered laboratory system and network. However, equipment functionality gaps remain a critical challenge for healthcare delivery. This study determined the functionality status of standardised laboratory analysers in Tanzania mainland and identified the drivers of non-functionality. Methods We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study to identify the causes of non-functionality of standardised chemistry, haematology, and urine analysers across mainland Tanzania. We assessed 3,044 analysers and used Pareto analysis to identify the primary drivers of non-functionality. Results Of the 3,044 standardised analysers assessed, 987 (32.4%) chemistry 1,308 (43.0%) haematology, and 749 (24.6%) urine) assessed; 397 (13.0%) were non-functional. Proportionally, urine analysers were the most non-functional (n=176/749, 23.5%), followed by chemistry (n=135/987, 13.7%), and haematology (n=86/1308, 6.6%) analysers, p<0.001. Urine analysers had significantly higher non-functional equipment (23.5%), followed by Chemistry analysers (13.7%), than Haematology analysers (6.6%), p<0.001. Equipment breakdown was the leading cause of non-functionality, accounting for 70.9% (61/86), 70.5% (124/176) and 60.0% (81/135) of the non-functional haematology, urine and chemistry analysers, respectively, among all causes identified for each analyser type. Conclusion Although the SMLEG 2018 implementation identified broad coverage of functional standardised laboratory equipment, persistent equipment breakdowns of more than 10% highlight a systemic, concerning gap that requires immediate corrective action to sustain high performance. Strengthening preventive maintenance, timely repair services and sustainable equipment lifecycle planning is critical to sustaining quality laboratory services for robust preventive and curative care.
n2f3b24e922ed: Purpose: To determine whether a cobalt-chrome genetic reactivity (CoGR) score - originally developed to identify patients at greater risk of developing adverse reaction to metal-on-metal hips - is associated with poorer patient-reported outcomes after knee arthroplasty (KA). Methods: In a prospective multicentre study, patients at a minimum two years post all cobalt-chrome KA were invited to research clinics. Participants provided samples for blood metal ion measurements and DNA sequencing and completed Forgotten Joint Scores (FJS). Component alignment was assessed on AP and lateral plain radiographs. The association between CoGR and FJS was assessed using regression adjusted for time since surgery, age, gender, BMI and tested for modification by blood cobalt. In a case-control analysis, CoGR scores of revised patients with histologically confirmed adverse reactions to metal debris (and specifically aseptic lymphocyte-dominated vasculitis-associated lesions (ALVAL)) were compared with controls (revised patients with no signs of ARMD and unrevised patients with FJS of 75 or more) using Firth logistic regression. Results: 376 patients were included: 312 unrevised patients and 64 patients who underwent revision. Each one-unit increase in CoGR score was associated with a 9.8 point lower FJS (95% confidence interval (CI) 4.2 to 15.4 points; p < 0.001). This increased to a 17.5 (9.4 to 25.5) point reduction per CoGR score unit in patients with blood cobalt above the median level. Comparing 28 ARMD cases (12 with ALVAL) with 177 controls, each one-unit CoGR increase was associated with odds ratios of 1.90 (CI 1.34 to 2.75) for ARMD and 3.05 (CI 1.89 to 5.34) for ALVAL. Conclusions: A higher CoGR score was associated with worse patient-reported outcome and higher odds of histologically confirmed adverse reaction to metal debris at revision. Adverse immune responses may be a more significant factor in unexplained pain after KA than is generally recognised.
n96b40ab29c06: Background: Hand hygiene is a key public health intervention for preventing infectious diseases, including respiratory and gastrointestinal infections. Although the COVID-19 pandemic improved awareness and compliance, sustained adherence remains a challenge, with evidence showing a decline in practice after outbreaks, particularly among young adults in high-contact settings such as universities. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of handwashing hygiene among university students at KCMC University, Moshi, Tanzania, in the post-COVID-19 era. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 students at KCMC University. Data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, which captured information on socio-demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding handwashing hygiene. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Associations between variables were assessed using logistic regression and multivariable analysis, and a p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results: A total of 380 students participated in the study, with a mean age of 23.5 {+/-} 3.5 years. More than half 209 (55.0%) were aged 18-23 years, while 203 (53.4%) were female. Most participants had access to hand hygiene facilities 338 (88.9%). 338 (88.9%) participants had good knowledge of hand hygiene but attitudes were mostly negative 193 (50.8%), and practices were suboptimal, with 201 (52.9%) showing poor hand hygiene practices. Good hand hygiene knowledge was associated with access to hand hygiene facilities (AOR=2.84, 95% CI: 1.25-6.42, p=0.012) and formal training on hand hygiene (AOR=3.48, 95% CI: 1.24-9.76, p=0.018). Positive attitudes were associated with being in the fourth year or above (AOR=2.12, 95% CI: 1.16-3.89, p=0.015). Good hand hygiene practices were associated with access to hand hygiene facilities (AOR=2.67, 95% CI: 1.18-6.01, p=0.018) and formal training on hand hygiene (AOR=2.98, 95% CI: 1.19-7.48, p=0.020). Conclusion: Although knowledge and awareness of handwashing hygiene were generally high among university students, inconsistencies between knowledge and actual practices were observed in the post-COVID-19 era. Strengthening health education programs and ensuring continuous access to handwashing facilities may improve adherence to proper hand hygiene practices among university students.
n76ec5d887337: Background: Recent work has brought large language models (LLMs) into clinical variant interpretation. In most existing approaches, the model is confined to text-level operations, retrieving, extracting, compacting, and summarizing heterogeneous evidence, while the genuine genetic evaluation is delegated to a separate deterministic engine. Other tools employ LLMs to mine functional evidence for a single ACMG criterion, to rerank a classifier's output, or to answer isolated variant questions. Integrative genetic reasoning, by contrast, demands multi-source evidence weighing for each variant, reconciliation of inheritance with observed zygosity and parental genotypes, joint interpretation of variants in the same gene, and the derivation of a case-level conclusion. Moreover, to protect patient privacy, this must be done on hospital premises. Methods: o build an end-to-end variant interpreter that runs on local infrastructure, we benchmarked 13 small language models (SLMs) on 150 multiple-choice genetics questions and selected Qwen3.5-9B. In IVA (Intelligent Variant Analyser), a four-stage pipeline, the model assigns ACMG/AMP criteria, applies de novo, dominant, recessive, and X-linked inheritance logic to trios, and writes a structured report, while deterministic code handles retrieval, phasing, point summation, citation checking, and formatting. We evaluated IVA on synthetic scenarios, 16 solved trios, and 327 solved singleton cases of visual impairment, on a single GPU. Results: On the benchmark, Qwen3.5-9B reached a mean accuracy of 0.81, compared with 0.89 for a 1.6-trillion-parameter cloud model. In the 16 trios, IVA reported every previously identified pathogenic, likely pathogenic, or uncertain-significance variant of interest (sensitivity 100%; precision 39.5%). In the 327 singleton cases, it recovered 93% of the expert-reported causative variants and classified 82% of them as pathogenic or likely pathogenic (precision 43%). Failures fell into four recurrent classes: omission, unverified mechanism, mismatch between reasoning and label, and arithmetic errors. Conclusions: A small language model running on local hardware can serve as the reasoning layer for case-level and trio-based variant interpretation when it is surrounded by deterministic safeguards. Because its outputs are not deterministic, analyst review and prospective multicenter validation remain necessary.
na32ad428f1ab: BCG is a well recognized old generic drug that can mold the human immune system through Immune Training. Broad basic science studies support Immune Training, but formal randomized placebo control trials are frequently lacking for confirmation of human benefits. Here we report on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial with up to 8 years of follow-up. The primary outcome was mean percent change from baseline in HbA1c. At year 5, HbA1c in the BCG group was reduced from baseline by 7.04% (P=0.0006) and at year 8 by 12.84% (P=0.0001), whereas HbA1c did not change from baseline in the placebo group at either time point. Longitudinal percentage changes in HbA1c from baseline using mixed model repeated measures analysis with a comparison of BCG versus Placebo arms was significant (p=0.0017). This shows durable long term improvements lowering of HbA1c only with BCG immunotherapy. Secondary outcomes were also significant. There was a statistically significant reduction in average insulin dose only in the BCG-treated group (P=0.024). Glycemic improvements occurred without recovery of C-peptide from negligible baseline levels, suggesting no pancreas contribution. Blood sugar values obtained from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) similarly showed BCG immunotherapy lowers blood sugars compared to the Placebo arm (P=0.0189). CGM data also showed BCG immunotherapy resulted in an up to 183.7% improvement over baseline in time spent in normoglycemia (blood sugar in the normal range of 70-99 mg/dL) (P=0.0391). A sensitivity analysis confirmed BCG specific reductions in HbA1c were robust and durable at least to Year 08 (P<0.0001). BCG was safe. These finding support improved blood sugar control through immune training of metabolism without a contribution of the pancreas even after long standing T1D. Trial registration: NCT02081326 .
n2bf81fe7db88: Current health risk assessments from thirdhand exposure to methamphetamine (meth) to occupants of contaminated residences when no cooking or use is still occurring assume that inhalation exposure is insignificant. After Wright et al. (2021) reported substantial meth concentrations in a contaminated residence, the present study was conducted to further test the hypothesis that concentrations were high enough to contribute to total occupant dose. Air sampling was conducted in contaminated residences that had been previously sampled for surface contamination. Samples were collected on personal sampling pumps in fixed locations on treated glass fiber filters is cassettes and analyzed by gas or liquid chromatography with mass spectroscopy. Sixty-nine samples were collected from eighteen residences for the study. Meth concentrations ranged from 0.02 to 15 ug/m3. Concentrations in supply air vents were significantly higher than in return vents or in ambient air. Residences with no HVAC systems (baseboard heat) had airborne concentrations similar to residences with HVAC systems turned off, and lower than when HVAC was on. Whether a residence was occupied or not did not show differences. All data from residences with HVAC had a significant correlation with surface concentrations (R2 = 0.61) but some factors that affected results were not determined in the study. In the context of the risk assessment and regulatory standard established by California and adopted in several other states, the inhalation exposure would approximately double total occupant dose for infants, and this population would exceed the California reference dose by approximately 100%. Further studies should be conducted to refine these estimates and determine the factors that influence airborne concentrations.
ndfc754781cf9: BACKGROUND: Federal policy now requires sponsors to submit diversity action plans for clinical trials, yet the modifiable features of trial design associated with enrolled composition remain poorly characterized. English-language proficiency requirements are written into eligibility criteria and recorded as free text in a public registry, making them visible and, in principle, amenable to revision, but their relationship to enrolled composition has been examined only within single disease areas and in small samples of trials. We examined whether these requirements and documented language accommodation were associated with the racial and ethnic composition of enrolled participants. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a cross-sectional study of interventional trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov with at least one US site and posted results, using a registry snapshot retrieved in October 2026. The primary cohort comprised the 44,487 trials with exclusively US sites, of which 21,924 (49.3%) reported baseline race and 17,434 (39.2%) reported baseline ethnicity with counts that reconciled with the posted denominator. Both exposures were classified from free-text eligibility criteria using regular expressions validated against independent physician review of 150 trials. For the English-language requirement classifier, sensitivity was 88.2% and specificity was 99.2%. The outcome was the trial-level proportion of enrolled participants in each category, analyzed using generalized linear models adjusted for intervention class, therapeutic area, sponsor, phase, enrollment, sites, start year, US Census region, and the population composition of the trial's site states. An English-language proficiency requirement appeared in 5,736 trials (12.9%); its prevalence rose from 7.4% of trials starting in 2010 to 26.2% in 2023 (odds ratio [OR] per decade 2.91, P<0.001), whereas documented accommodation, an eligibility statement allowing participation in a language other than English (Spanish in 99.9% of flagged trials), remained rare (788 trials, 1.8%). The requirement was associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.77-0.93, P=0.001) and Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91, P<0.001), with no evidence of an association for White participants (OR=0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.04, P=0.75). Documented accommodation was associated with a higher proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants (OR=3.23, 95% CI 2.82-3.71, P<0.001). Geographic adjustment did not change the statistical significance of the requirement associations and attenuated the accommodation association. The main limitations were the cross-sectional design, which precludes causal inference; the restriction of enrollment analyses to trials reporting baseline demographics, which were more recent than those without such reporting; and possible misclassification of automatically classified exposures. CONCLUSIONS: English-language proficiency requirements became more than three times as common between 2010 and 2023 and were associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants. Less common documented language accommodation was associated with a higher enrolled proportion of Hispanic/Latinx participants. Because these criteria are investigator-written and publicly recorded, they may be a tractable target for improving enrollment equity, although whether revising them changes who enrolls requires prospective evaluation
ne63e8c8e4fc3: Autism is highly heritable, yet many cases remain genetically unsolved even after short-read sequencing (SRS). Long-read sequencing (LRS) increases sensitivity for pathogenic variant discovery, especially for complex structural variants (SVs) in repetitive regions missed by SRS. However, LRS largely relies on blood-derived DNA; whether saliva can support genome-wide LRS at population scale remains to be seen. We report the first systematic evaluation of saliva-derived DNA for genome-wide LRS in autism, benchmarking 105 new saliva samples against 68 new blood samples and integrating 189 previously published LRS blood samples to expand the autism cohort and improve ultra-rare pathogenic variant discovery. A matched blood-saliva quad provided direct comparisons of variant detection between sample sources. Saliva samples contained substantially more nonhuman DNA than blood (mean 10% versus 0.005% of reads), reducing mean effective genome coverage from an estimated 28X to 24X after removal of nonhuman reads, compared with 34X in blood samples. Despite this reduction, saliva and blood samples yielded comparable numbers of validated (22,591 versus 23,064) and rare (209 versus 213) SVs per sample, which was also observed in the quad when matching coverage. Saliva LRS identified four new pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants missed by SRS. We report variants affecting MECP2 , DNMT3A , CHD8 , LMBRD2 , POGZ , and PHF3 ; four additional candidates with potential relevance to autism; and an increase of diagnostic yield of 9-18%. Saliva-derived DNA support blood-comparable discovery of pathogenic variants missed by SRS, including SVs, with increased sequencing coverage compensating for nonhuman DNA contamination and reduced assembly contiguity, thus showing saliva DNA collection as a feasible strategy for large-scale LRS studies of patients and population-scale sequencing of cohorts.
nd26c294dc732: Background: Pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM) is a major complication of chronic right ventricular pacing and develops in up to 25% of patients. Reliable prediction of PICM may facilitate individualized pacing strategy selection; however, currently available approaches demonstrate limited discriminative performance. This study aimed to develop and validate machine learning (ML) models for predicting PICM in patients with atrioventricular block (AVB) underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction. Methods: In this multicenter prospective study derived from the RISK-PICM registry (January 2002 to January 2026), 125 patients with AVB who underwent pacemaker implantation were analyzed. PICM was defined as a ?10% reduction in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) resulting in an LVEF <50%. Four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost, were trained using stratified 4-fold cross-validation with hyperparameter optimization and model discrimination was evaluated. Results: PICM developed in 41 patients (32.8%) during a median follow-up of 4.8 years. Male sex, pre-implant minimum QTc interval, and post-implant maximum QRS duration were significantly associated with PICM in univariable Cox regression. XGBoost achieved the highest discriminative performance (AUROC 0.831; sensitivity 0.805; specificity 0.845). Feature importance analysis identified baseline LVEF and post-implant maximum QRS duration as the most influential features. Model-derived risk stratification significantly differentiated high-risk and low-risk groups on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P < 0.001). Conclusions: ML-based models, particularly XGBoost, demonstrated clinically meaningful performance for PICM and may support individualized pacing strategy selection in patients with AVB and underlying heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.
n6f4289ea2ec6: Purpose: to introduce a novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique, MUSLIS MRI (muscle and lipid suppression), that generates two co-registered 3D sets of images in a single acquisition: one set with lipid signal suppression (MUSLIS1) and a second set with muscle signal suppression (MUSLIS2). Materials and Methods: Numerical simulations based on Bloch equations were performed to optimize the sequence parameters; the MP2RAGE sequence was employed for the implementation of MUSLIS imaging. MRI experiments were performed in vivo at 3 T. Quantitative measurements of signal contrast were carried out on MUSLIS1 and MUSLIS2. Various combination images and T1 parametric maps of the thighs were generated from the two co-registered 3D sets. Results and Discussion: Optimal sequence parameters to achieve lipid suppression in one dataset (MUSLIS1) and muscle suppression in the other dataset (MUSLIS2) were determined by numerical simulations. MUSLIS imaging was validated in vivo at 3 T: MUSLIS1 images and MUSLIS2 images displayed excellent lipid and muscle suppression, respectively. The values of the signal contrast between subcutaneous lipids and muscle, as well as between bone marrow lipids and muscle reached values close to 0.8. Thus, MUSLIS would allow for tissue characterization of lesion/masses and direct visualization of the adipose tissue. Combination images, generated from these two intrinsically co-registered sets of images (MUSLIS1 and MUSLIS2), displayed different contrasts and improved signal characteristics, such as mitigation of signal inhomogeneities. The development of MUSLIS imaging for musculoskeletal imaging followed the concept introduced with the FLAWS, an MRI sequence designed for brain MR imaging to generate two 3D sets of images, one with white matter suppression and the other with cerebrospinal fluid suppression. Similarly to FLAWS, which provides T1 maps of the brain, MUSLIS imaging yields T1 parametric maps of the musculoskeletal system. Furthermore, the unique characteristics of the combination images make MUSLIS imaging a potentially attractive technique at field strengths higher than 3 T. Conclusion: The proof-of-concept of a novel approach to musculoskeletal imaging, MUSLIS MRI, is proposed here and demonstrated by numerical simulations and MRI experiments performed in vivo at 3 T. Keywords: MRI, muscle, lipids, musculoskeletal imaging, high field MRI, fat suppression, FLAWS MRI, MP2RAGE, MUSLIS, inversion recovery, adipose tissue, bone marrow, subcutaneous fat, T1 mapping, 3 T, 7 T, neuromuscular disorders, metabolic diseases, muscular dystrophy.
n609dad838c02: Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.
n98c3c8223f6e: C9orf72 encodes a protein that is important for both typical neurodevelopment and homeostatic processes across the lifespan. Pathogenic C9orf72 repeat expansions constitute the most common genetic cause of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD). Collectively, preclinical models and clinical neuroimaging studies have observed smaller thalamic volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD, including in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 repeat expansion carriers across 18 to 30 years old, supportive of potential neurodevelopmental origins. However, it is unknown whether asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers demonstrate volume differences in specific thalamic nuclei, as reported in older asymptomatic carriers and symptomatic patients; if so, normative transcriptomic patterns could reveal relevant neurodevelopmental and/or FTLD-related neurodegenerative processes. This study investigated volumetric MRI differences of the thalamic nuclei in asymptomatic young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers, and examined spatial associations with normative thalamic transcriptomics from 8 weeks post-conception through middle age. Young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers (n=72) and non-carriers (n=48) were enrolled in the Frontotemporal Dementia Prevention Initiative across Europe, Canada, and the USA (ages: 18-30 years; sex: 57% female). Spatial associations between young adult thalamic nuclei volumes and normative transcriptomics from the Allen Human Brain Atlas were examined using complementary data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches. Spatial expression patterns of transcripts of interest were characterized across prenatal and postnatal neurodevelopment using BrainSpan data. Smaller volumes of the pulvinar, mediodorsal, and lateral nuclei were observed in young adult C9orf72 expansion carriers compared to non-carriers. These nuclei showed higher normative expression of transcripts involved concurrently in neurodevelopmental and C9orf72-associated FTLD neurodegenerative processes (including lysosomal, autophagic, and small GTPase functions), and lower normative expression of CALB1, a marker of prenatal human thalamic development. Normative expression of CALB2 (another human thalamic development marker) yielded positive correlations with C9orf72 across prenatal development to adulthood. These findings identify candidate transcripts that may provide insight into the molecular architecture leading to smaller thalamic nuclei volumes in C9orf72-associated FTLD.
nb11978c8e499: Background We aimed to characterize substance use patterns, and their correlates, among adults with and without HIV at two healthcare facilities in Cape Town, South Africa. Methods We recruited adults with and without HIV from two primary healthcare facilities. We assessed alcohol use with the AUDIT-C and other substance use with the WHO-ASSIST questionnaires. We classified participants with no lifetime drug use and no or low-risk alcohol use as "low risk" and fitted latent class models among remaining participants to identify additional substance use patterns. We used multinomial logistic regression to examine factors associated with substance use patterns. Results Among 602 participants, 265 (44.0%) were "low risk". Latent class analysis among the remaining 337 identified three patterns: "higher-risk alcohol use" (N=168; 27.9%), "cannabis use" (universal cannabis use with mixed alcohol risk; N=114; 18.9%), and "mixed illicit drug use" (predominantly no or low-risk alcohol use with use of multiple drugs; N=55; 9.1%). Participants younger than 45 years were less likely to be in the low-risk group. Male sex was associated with lower probability of the low-risk group and higher probability of the higher-risk alcohol use and cannabis use classes. HIV was associated with higher probability of higher-risk alcohol use. One facility had a substantially higher probability of mixed illicit drug use. Conclusions We identified distinct higher-risk substance use profiles that varied strongly by age, sex, and facility. These findings support integrating alcohol and substance use screening and management into primary care and tailoring responses to local substance use patterns.
n3704350a4d63: Objectives: Heatwaves drive surges in acute care demand, yet heat-health action plans (HHAPs) lack tools to scale emergency care responses. This study validated a forecasting tool for heatwave-related emergency department (ED) demand across four clusters comprising the emergency care network of Ticino Canton, Switzerland. Methods: This retrospective, ecological, time-series study modeled daily mean temperature and ED presentations using a distributed lag non-linear model framework with autoregressive and calendar adjustment components. The model was trained on summers (June-August) 2016-2024 and tested on summer 2025, defining heatwaves as daily mean temperature >25 {degrees}C for [≥]3 consecutive days. Results: A non-linear temperature-demand association was shown across the clusters, with ED visits increasing at higher temperatures. Model fit varied across clusters (R2 0.389-0.672), and the reference model consistently outperformed naive baselines. During two heatwaves in 2025, prediction errors remained within acceptable ranges. Baseline demand, heatwave occurrence, and model performance varied substantially within the canton. Conclusions: These findings have implications for the design of HHAPs, suggesting that emergency care preparedness should rely on locally calibrated demand forecast rather than standardized activation protocols.
n846445d070b4: Standard cardiac biomarkers such as ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, and strain compress complex three-dimensional heart dynamics into a small set of predefined measurements, leaving clinically important heterogeneity unrecognised. Here we propose a personalised normative cardiac framework in which each individual is compared to a digital twin representing expected healthy cardiac function given their age, sex, and body habitus. We show that structured patterns of deviation from these normative twins, discovered through systematic exploration of a generative cardiac dynamics space, constitute novel dynamic phenotypes that are not captured by conventional biomarkers. Applied independently to two UK Biobank cardiac cohorts with distinct shape representation, a 128-dimensional four-chamber statistical shape descriptor (HeartSSM, n = 52,365) and a 64-dimensional deep generative latent space from a conditional variational mesh autoencoder (MeshHeart cVAE, n = up to 39,376), we identify reproducible, continuous deviation-from-normative-twin scores (three discrete deviation phenotypes in the HeartSSM cohort) that improve cardiovascular risk stratification beyond ejection fraction, ventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and strain. The strongest effect was seen for incident atrial fibrillation among individuals with preserved ejection fraction (at least 50%): incremental C-index delta C = +0.068 (5-fold cross-validated delta C = +0.063; likelihood-ratio P = 3.3 x 10^-8), with a separate, smaller effect for incident stroke in the same preserved-EF subgroup in the independent MeshHeart cVAE representation (which showed no signal for atrial fibrillation) (delta C = +0.024, P = 2.6 x 10^-4). Both effects were checked against placebo controls in which the deviation scores were replaced by Gaussian noise. To test whether the normative twin generalises beyond UK Biobank's specific scanning and processing pipeline, we applied the MeshHeart cVAE normative twin, unmodified, to an independent external cohort of healthy volunteers imaged at a different hospital (GenScan/Hammersmith, n = 315): deviation scores in this cohort were of comparable magnitude to the UK Biobank healthy reference (ratio of means = 1.09; Mann-Whitney P = 1.4 x 10^-5), indicating that the normative twin captures cross-site-transferable structure rather than a scanner- or pipeline-specific artefact. Our findings suggest that cardiac phenotyping can move beyond predefined measurements toward data-driven dynamic phenotypes that better capture the heterogeneity underlying cardiovascular disease risk, even among individuals whose ejection fraction appears normal.
n884afb70a1b5: Background: Whether ethnoracial differences in cerebral small vessel disease (cSVD) appear in multimarker burden, particular MRI manifestations, or both, and how they relate to Life's Essential 8 (LE8) cardiovascular health and cognition, remain unclear. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 44,982 participants and an age- and sex-matched subsample of 1,426 with reviewed lacune and cerebral microbleed (CMB) ratings. White, South Asian, Black, Chinese and Mixed participants were compared on 0-2 (white matter hyperintensity [WMH]/enlarged perivascular space [ePVS]) and 0-4 (adding CMB and lacunes) composite scores and each marker. LE8 was related to WMH and composite burden, and cognitive means were compared by group. Models were age-, sex- and center-adjusted with false-discovery-rate correction. Results: Both composite scores differed across groups (0-2: P=0.00010; 0-4: P=0.0011), with greater burden in Black than South Asian (0-4: OR 1.66; 95% CI, 1.21-2.28) and Chinese participants (OR 2.36; 1.51-3.70), whereas Black-White contrasts were not detected. Black participants had higher WMH volume than White participants (=0.209; 0.110-0.308), robust to deprivation adjustment and segmentation method; South Asian participants had fewer ePVS (0.82; 0.72-0.93). No ethnoracial-group differences in lacune or CMB counts were detected after correction. Higher LE8 was associated with lower WMH volume (0.13 per SD; 0.17 to 0.09) and lower two-marker burden (OR 0.89 per SD; 0.87-0.91) without detected ethnoracial moderation. Black participants, who had the least favorable LE8 scores, and South Asian participants had lower global cognition than White participants (z 0.76 and 0.57 versus 0.24) despite differing WMH profiles; the pooled WMH-cognition association was null. Conclusions: Ethnoracial differences in multimarker cSVD burden were evident but marker-dependent: WMH showed the clearest Black-White difference; focal-lesion contrasts were inconclusive. Better cardiovascular health related to lower WMH and aggregate cSVD burden across groups, whereas cognitive differences did not track cSVD burden, supporting prospective prevention and cognition studies.
n1cc32c3abc78: Objective: To identify demographic and daily cognitive, affective, and contextual predictors of headache-related interference with activity and concentration in a smartphone-based migraine cohort, using statistical models appropriate to the ordinal structure of patient-reported interference. Background: Migraine burden extends beyond headache to encompass cognitive and affective disturbance, yet most disability instruments summarize functioning retrospectively and cannot capture day-to-day variability in interference. Ecological momentary assessment addresses this limitation, yet few studies have examined cognitive and affective correlates of interference independent of pain intensity or have modeled interference using methods that respect its ordinal, non-equal-interval structure. Methods: From May 2025 to April 2026, adult participants were enrolled in this prospective, decentralized observational study via specialty clinics and social media campaigns. Eligibility required fulfilling ICHD-3 diagnostic criteria for migraine using a validated electronic survey and experiencing between 3 and 20 monthly headache days. Enrolled individuals recorded daily smartphone diary entries and performed three brief cognitive tests over a 30-day monitoring period. Daily interference with activities and concentration were captured on 5-point ordinal scales and analyzed via cumulative link mixed-effects models incorporating participant-specific random intercepts. Predictor selection across nested specifications relied on likelihood ratio testing and Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) metrics, prioritizing the more parsimonious model when goodness-of-fit was comparable. Results: The analytic sample comprised 1,267 headache-day observations from 143 participants. In the final models, brain fog (OR = 2.49 for activity, 3.19 for concentration), forgetfulness (OR = 1.48, 1.65), and mood disturbance (OR = 1.19, 1.31) were each independently associated with both outcomes (all p < 0.01), while age, sex, and employment status showed no significant association with either. Sleep quality (OR = 0.86) and anticipated next-day enjoyment (OR = 0.81) provided additional explanatory value for activity interference (p < 0.05) but not for concentration interference, for which the three-predictor model of brain fog, forgetfulness, and mood alone was retained as the most parsimonious final model. Conclusions: Cognitive and affective symptoms, rather than demographic or socioeconomic characteristics, are the primary correlates of headache-related functional interference in this cohort. Activity and concentration interference are explained by partially distinct sets of daily influences, supporting the clinical value of assessing cognitive and affective symptoms alongside conventional pain-focused evaluation.
nbdc1a9df70a3: Background: Lead is a cumulative environmental toxicant for which no safe level of exposure has been identified, and pregnant women and their fetuses are particularly vulnerable because lead readily crosses the placenta and can be mobilised from maternal bone stores. Bangladesh conducted its first nationally representative blood lead testing among pregnant women through the 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS), but a detailed, multi-domain analysis of the determinants of elevated blood lead level (BLL) among this population has not yet been reported. Methods: We conducted a secondary cross-sectional analysis of 1,928 pregnant women aged 15-49 years with complete data from the women's dataset of Bangladesh MICS 2025. Elevated BLL was defined as [≥]5 g/dL. Survey-weighted logistic regression was used to estimate unadjusted and adjusted odds ratios (aOR) for co-exposure to arsenic, cadmium and mercury and sociodemographic and socioeconomic covariates. Slope Index of Inequality (SII) as well as Relative Index of Inequality (RII) were used to quantify wealth-related inequality. Population attributable fractions (PAF) were estimated for three counterfactual scenarios, and adaptive least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used as a sensitivity analysis. Results: Elevated BLL was present among 6.2% of participants. In the adjusted model, a 2-fold rise in blood cadmium was associated with higher odds of elevated BLL (aOR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.21-1.96), whereas a 2-fold rise in blood mercury (aOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.48-0.83), rural residence (aOR: 0.55; 95% CI: 0.32-0.94), secondary education (aOR: 0.49; 95% CI: 0.28-0.85) and post-secondary education (aOR: 0.22; 95% CI: 0.11-0.46) were associated with lower odds. Belonging to progressively wealthier quintiles was associated with markedly higher odds, BLL rising to an aOR of 10.32 (95% CI: 4.41-24.15) for the richest versus poorest quintile. The RII was 8.59 (95% CI: 4.24-17.40) and the SII was 0.159 (95% CI: 0.101-0.218), indicating a substantial pro-rich gradient in elevated BLL. Counterfactual scenarios suggested that shifting the population to secondary-level education could reduce the prevalence of elevated BLL by 52.9% (95% CI: 20.6-72.0) and shifting to rural residence by 24.3% (95% CI: 1.4-41.9). Adaptive LASSO variable selection produced estimates consistent in direction and magnitude with the fully adjusted model. Conclusion: In this national sample, approximately one out of every 16 pregnant women had blood lead levels that met or exceeded the action threshold set by the World Health Organization, with this issue being particularly prevalent among wealthier, urban, and less-educated women, and was compounded by co-exposure to cadmium. In Bangladesh, the typical pattern observed for maternal and child health indicators does not align with the inverse relationship found between household wealth and lead exposure.
